title: Parity-driven pin canary with drift-aware rebalancer
creator: Riley Patel
description: Introduce a parity-first canary workflow for model revisions that are deployed behind customer pins. The feature will perform paired-request A/Bs against the pinned baseline and the candidate revision, enforce parity and safety gates across behavioral and infra signals, and enable a drift-aware traffic rebalancer that automatically reduces candidate weight when statistical divergence is detected. This aims to reduce noisy rollouts, prevent customer-facing regressions behind pins, and make pinned upgrades low-friction for platform and tenant teams.
acceptance_criteria: Platform exposes a 'Parity Canaries' toggle on pin configuration and an API to create parity canary jobs for a pinned revision.
Paired-request harness returns both baseline and candidate outputs with a single request ID and stores diffs in the canary telemetry table.
Automatic drift detector computes real-time JS divergence and semantic similarity (embedding cosine) for canary cohorts and surfaces a single composite divergence score.
Configurable gates: behavioral parity (QA prompts pass rate >= 99%), latency tail (p95 within budget), error rate (<= baseline + 0.1%), and quality regressions (regression rate <= 0.5%).

Drift-aware rebalancer automatically steps down candidate traffic by configured steps (example: 50% -> 25% -> 0%) when composite divergence exceeds threshold for N consecutive windows, and records rollback events in audit logs.
Dashboard widgets for per-pin canaries, per-tenant micro-cohort breakdowns, and trend alerts are available in Console for the release.
Playbook and runbook with rollback and escalation steps published to Confluence and linked in the canary UI.
End-to-end latency overhead for parity mode <= 10% for 95% of requests (measured under typical load profiles).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Infra & API): implement paired request API and canary job scheduler; enable internal feature flag.
Phase 1 (Pilot): enable parity canaries for 3 internal tenants and 2 strategic customers; run synthetic prompt suites + live traffic micro-cohorts.
Phase 2 (Gradual Open): expose UI toggle in Console behind permission; allow opt-in for pinned revisions with default conservative thresholds.
Phase 3 (Auto-Rebalance On): enable drift-aware rebalancer as opt-out for Dedicated customers after 2 production months of stable runs.
Rollback policy: immediate step-down to 0% for candidate if any hard safety gate fails (safety heuristics or severe error spike).
test_plan: Unit tests for paired-request path, schema compatibility, and audit logging.
Integration tests: simulate mixed-tenant load, ensure KV cache reuse not polluted, validate p95 latency budgets.
E2E tests: reproduce known regression cases from historical evals to ensure detection sensitivity (false negative rate < 2%).
Chaos test: inject transient GPU stalls and network flaps to validate rebalancer does not oscillate under noisy signals.
Privacy/regression test: ensure candidate outputs storage obeys pin-level data retention and encryption policies.
metrics: Behavioral parity pass rate (fraction of prompts that meet semantic-match rules and QA tests)
Composite divergence score (0-1) combining JS divergence and embedding drift
Latency p50/p95/p99 for baseline and candidate
False positive / false negative detection rates on synthetic regression suite
Per-tenant cost delta (tokens and infra) while parity mode enabled
comments: 2026-02-25 Riley Patel: Ticket created. Initial scoping with Eng and Research. Goal is to reduce pinned-upgrade regressions reported by customers.

2026-02-28 Alex Chen: Proposed paired-request API prototype sketched; noted cache isolation concerns when running baseline+candidate sequentially within same request. Asked Runtime team for cache control knob.
2026-03-03 Samir Gupta (Eng): Backend prototype completed. Using request-level cache key separation to avoid KV contamination. Benchmarks show ~6% median latency overhead on 8k context models.

2026-03-05 Maya Li (Research): Suggested composite divergence combining JS divergence on token distributions and cosine similarity on redwood-embeddings to catch semantic drift cases that token-level metrics miss.

2026-03-07 PM review: Decided to make rebalancer conservative by default (3-window confirmation) and expose tuning knobs in Console. Added requirement for audit trail for any automatic traffic reduction.
2026-03-10 Ops feedback: Alerting thresholds must tie into SLA on-call; added explicit runbook steps for on-call to pause rebalancer and manually inspect artifacts.
notes: Trade-offs considered: synchronous paired-requests vs shadowing. Synchronous provides simpler parity attribution but increases tail latency; shadowing is lower latency but reduces signal parity fidelity.
Decision: start with synchronous paired-requests for pinned upgrades where correctness is critical; evaluate an async shadow hybrid later.
Potential follow-ups: per-tenant sensitivity thresholds, ML-based anomaly detector to reduce false positives, and support for multi-variant experiments behind pins.
